prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Pasadena, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1188; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is not named on the policy and does not live with the policyholder.
text: Officers were dispatched to a two-vehicle collision in Pasadena, Texas, where a low-speed head-on impact occurred in the roadway. Driver 1 was seated behind the wheel of the eastbound sedan at the time of the crash, and Passenger was also seated in that vehicle. Driver 1 told officers of neck pain and stiffness following the impact, and the injury complaint is consistent with the direction and force of the collision. Driver 2, operating the westbound pickup, stated that the crash occurred as Driver 1 described. Two witnesses on the sidewalk gave statements that matched both drivers' accounts, and scene photographs show front-end damage to both vehicles consistent with the impact. Neither vehicle showed prior damage in the same areas. Driver 1 was identified as an occupant of the sedan by officers and both witnesses. Driver 1 provided proof of insurance on the sedan, which lists a different named insured. Officers observed no signs of impairment. Both vehicles were towed from the scene.
